For me growing up as a kid, when I first discovered stories that blended scifi and fantasy, my young mind was blown. There was a pc game where you go around slaying dragons and casting spells, only to learn that the final boss of the game are crash landed aliens and you must kill them with lazer guns and now I cant divorce the two genres.

Do you like when the two are mixed? If so, why? Why not? Is it overdone or not done enough? Do you have a favorite example of this mix?
"You got Scifi in my Fantasy!" "And you got Fantasy in my Scifi!"

I do enjoy a mix of sci-fi and fantasy when its done well. A perfect example is Star Wars.

The Force is essentially magic, it has its own will, it can be used to defy the laws of the natural sciences to the point where it can even create life ie, Sithspawn however it isn't called magic, and while all life is in some way "connected" to the Force, not everyone can use it. Thus this allows for a Universe in which Technology advances as it would in a world without magic yet magic still plays some role. Furthermore while there is no limits to its use, a lot of the more refined methods of manipulating the force require heavy rituals and immense study.

In some ways, the Star Wars series handles magic better than fantasy series such as Harry Potter. In Harry Potter magic can seemingly do everything and yet nothing. A perfect example is the time turner which can turn back time but for some reason in later books doesn't make an appearance at all when it could be VITAL resource. Whereas in Star Wars, the Sith develop a thought bomb which required IMMENSE power from several Sith Lords as well as a complex ritual to boot.

Thats the kind of meld of sci-fi and fantasy that I enjoy, the majority either sci fi / fantasy and a minority of the other. An equal meld just bothers me.

My favorite sci-fi works have always had a very fantasy-ish side to them. I think my favorite sci-fi series, The Ender Saga, would be a great example of this. It starts out realistic enough with its advanced militarization and impeding doom at the hands of an alien race, but immediately within its sequels you get a glimpse of the lives of an alien race that is heavily into tree-worship and the differing human tribes that colonize the Hundred Worlds.

Its definitely not high fantasy; it doesn't have dragons or wizards, but I think there's still a lot of magic to it.
I always thought the spiritual aspect of the later Ender books was a bit heavy-handed. I think Orson Scott Card is at his best when his writing isn't really trying to shoehorn in his religious views.
Its a lot easier to digest if you think of it only as lore.

I don't mind the mixing. But the world has to have consistent rules and boundaries. If anything becomes possible, then the writing tends to get sloppy, the world tends to be poorly justified and their is no more struggle. Just deus ex machina.

I actually prefer the two genres to remain separate. I don't care if writers meld the two, but I'll always view the melding as inferior to pure sci-fi or fantasy.

There is one exception for me and that's the shadowrun universe. It has a special place in my heart.
Shadowrun is awesome. I've been the PC version, and just recently purchased it for Droid. I'm thoroughly enjoying playing it on my phone on the way home.

I don't see a problem with it, because as Clarke's Third Law states, "Any sufficiently advanced technology is indistinguishable from magic." Heck, they have a setting in Pathfinder that is effectively "Barbarians vs. Aliens", so why not, right? I think so long as it's done properly and not just played solely for laughs or treated like SRS BSNS it can work out fine.
after a certain line, horror, sci fi, and fantasy all fall into one fantastical category. mixing them is half the fun.

I don't really mind that the two mix...but...I have found it frustrating when making the occasional trip to a bookstore to look for something strictly space related. There is usually quiet a bit involving magic/dragons etc. (I like as well) and not much along the lines of future realism. I suppose I am trying to narrow down my search too much.
